• Waste utilization in biofuel production is important because it helps in the efficient use of

questions.question: Define lubricity and explain why lubricity additives are needed in modern jet fuels.
questions.solution_html:
• Lubricity is the ability of a fuel to provide adequate lubrication between moving metal surfaces
  • reducing friction and wear in fuel system components such as pumps and injectors.
  • In modern jet fuels, lubricity additives are needed because highly refined fuels (with low sulfur
  • and aromatic content) naturally have poor lubricating properties. This can lead to increased
  • wear, scuffing, and damage to fuel system parts. Therefore, lubricity additives are added to
  • improve the fuel’s ability to protect components, ensuring smooth operation, reduced
  • maintenance, and longer service life of the engine system. (definition (1 mark) and Two points
  • explanation (2 marks))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss on total additive sulphur in aviation fuels.
questions.solution_html:
• Total additive sulphur in aviation fuels refers to the sulphur content present in the fuel due to
  • naturally occurring sulphur compounds and, in some cases, from additive components. In
  • aviation turbine fuels, sulphur is not intentionally added for performance; instead, its level is
  • strictly controlled within specified limits. The presence of sulphur is important because
  • excessive sulphur can lead to corrosion of engine parts and formation of harmful combustion
  • products such as sulphur oxides, which contribute to environmental pollution. However, very
  • low sulphur content may reduce natural lubricity of the fuel. Therefore, maintaining an
  • optimum, limited sulphur content is essential to balance engine protection, fuel performance
  • and environmental considerations. (Any 3 points give (3 marks))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: State any three chemical properties of Aviation Turbine Fuel.
questions.solution_html:
• Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) exhibits important chemical properties that ensure safe and

questions.question: Examine the limitations of hydrogen as an aviation fuel.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the limitations of hydrogen as an aviation fuel.
  • Hydrogen has potential as a clean aviation fuel, but it has several important limitations. One
  • major issue is its low volumetric energy density, which means it occupies a much larger volume
  • than conventional jet fuel, requiring bulky and specially designed storage tanks. It must be
  • stored either at very high pressures or in liquid form at extremely low temperatures (cryogenic
  • conditions), making storage and handling complex and costly. Hydrogen also has high
  • flammability and requires strict safety measures to prevent leakage and fire hazards. In
  • addition, the current aviation infrastructure is not compatible with hydrogen, requiring major
  • modifications to aircraft design, fuel systems, and refuelling facilities. Finally, large-scale
  • production of hydrogen, especially green hydrogen, is still expensive and energy-intensive
  • limiting its widespread adoption in aviation. (Any 3 points give full credits)
  • Short Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Outline anaerobic digestion for biogas production.
questions.solution_html:
• Outline anaerobic digestion for biogas production.
  • Anaerobic digestion is a biological process in which organic matter such as animal dung
  • agricultural waste, and food waste is decomposed by microorganisms in the absence of oxygen
  • to produce biogas. The process takes place in an airtight digester and results in the formation
  • of biogas (mainly methane and carbon dioxide) and a nutrient-rich residue called digestate.
  • The process occurs in four main stages. Hydrolysis is the first step, where complex organic
  • materials like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats are broken down into simpler soluble
  • compounds. This is followed by acidogenesis, in which these products are converted into
  • volatile fatty acids, alcohols, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide by acid-forming bacteria. The third
  • stage, acetogenesis, converts these intermediate products into acetic acid, hydrogen, and carbon
  • dioxide. Finally, in methanogenesis, methanogenic bacteria convert acetic acid and hydrogen
  • into methane and carbon dioxide, which form the main components of biogas.
  • Anaerobic digestion is carried out under controlled conditions of temperature, pH, and moisture
  • to ensure efficient microbial activity. The biogas produced is used as a renewable fuel for
  • cooking, heating, and electricity generation, while the digestate is used as an organic fertilizer.
  • Thus, anaerobic digestion is an eco-friendly method for waste management and sustainable
  • energy production. (Any seven required points give (7 marks))
questions.final_answer: energy production. (Any seven required points give )
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Illustrate a suitable production technology for an ethanol plant designed for low capital investment and simpler operation.
questions.solution_html:
• investment and simpler operation.
  • A suitable production technology for an ethanol plant with low capital investment and simple
  • operation is the dry milling process. In this method, the entire grain (such as corn) is used
  • without separating its components, making the process economical and less complex compared
  • to wet milling.
  • In the dry milling process, the raw material is first cleaned and ground into flour (meal). The
  • ground material is then mixed with water to form a slurry, followed by liquefaction, where
  • enzymes (like α-amylase) break down starch into shorter chains. This is followed by
  • saccharification, where enzymes such as glucoamylase convert starch into fermentable sugars
  • (glucose). The resulting mash undergoes fermentation using yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
  • producing ethanol and carbon dioxide. After fermentation, the mixture is subjected to
  • distillation to separate ethanol, and further dehydration is carried out to obtain fuel-grade
  • ethanol.
  • The advantages of this technology include low initial investment, simpler equipment, ease of
  • operation, and suitability for small- to medium-scale plants. Although it produces fewer co
  • products compared to wet milling, it is widely preferred where cost and operational simplicity
  • are important. (Any 5 relevant points give full credit)
questions.final_answer: are important. (Any 5 relevant points give full credit)

questions.question: Identify the advantages of AV gas fuel over turbine engine fuel.
questions.solution_html:
• Aviation gasoline (AvGas) offers several advantages over turbine engine fuel (ATF) when used
  • in piston-engine aircraft. It has a higher-octane number, which provides excellent anti-knock
  • properties and ensures smooth combustion in high-compression piston engines. AvGas also
  • has better volatility, allowing easy vaporization and reliable engine starting, especially under
  • cold conditions. It ensures uniform air–fuel mixing, leading to efficient combustion and stable
  • engine performance. Additionally, AvGas produces cleaner combustion with fewer deposits in
  • piston engines compared to heavier fuels. It is well-suited for lightweight aircraft engines
  • offering good throttle response and operational simplicity. Overall, AvGas is specifically
  • optimized for piston engines, providing reliability, efficiency, and consistent performance
  • under varying flight conditions. (Any 5 points give full credit)
questions.final_answer: under varying flight conditions. (Any 5 points give full credit)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List the advantages and limitations of using SAF in modern aviation.
questions.solution_html:
• List the advantages and limitations of using SAF in modern aviation.
  • Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) offers several advantages in modern aviation. It significantly
  • reduces greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional jet fuel, helping to mitigate
  • climate change. SAF is produced from renewable resources such as biomass, waste oils, and
  • agricultural residues, promoting sustainability and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. It is
  • compatible with existing aircraft engines and infrastructure (drop-in fuel), requiring minimal
  • modifications. SAF also contains lower sulphur and aromatic content, resulting in cleaner
  • combustion, reduced particulate emissions, and improved air quality. Additionally, it supports
  • waste utilization and contributes to a circular economy.
  • However, SAF also has certain limitations. The high production cost makes it less
  • economically competitive than conventional fuels. There is limited large-scale availability due
  • to constraints in feedstock supply and production capacity. Some SAF pathways may face
  • feedstock sustainability issues and competition with food resources. The production processes
  • can be energy-intensive, and achieving consistent fuel quality can be challenging. Furthermore
  • widespread adoption requires policy support, infrastructure development, and technological
  • advancements. Thus, while SAF is environmentally beneficial, economic and scalability
  • challenges limit its current usage.
  • (Any 3 points from advantages and limitations give (3.5 marks) each)
questions.final_answer: (Any 3 points from advantages and limitations give each)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: State the hydrotreating process used in the manufacture of ATF, including operating conditions, reactions involved, and improvements in fuel quality
questions.solution_html:
• conditions, reactions involved, and improvements in fuel quality.
  • Hydrotreating is a key refinery process used in the manufacture of aviation turbine fuel (ATF)
  • to improve its quality and ensure it meets strict aviation specifications. In this process, the
  • kerosene fraction obtained from crude oil distillation is mixed with hydrogen and passed over
  • a catalyst –molybdenum or nickel–molybdenum on alumina) at high
  • temperature and pressure. The hydrogen reacts with impurities such as sulphur, nitrogen
  • oxygen compounds, and unsaturated hydrocarbons, converting them into stable products like
  • hydrogen sulphide and ammonia, which are then removed. Hydrotreating improves the fuel’s
  • thermal stability, reduces corrosiveness, lowers sulphur content, and enhances combustion
  • characteristics. After the reaction, the treated fuel is cooled, gases are separated, and the
  • purified ATF is recovered, meeting the required standards for safe and efficient aircraft
  • operation. (statement about hydrotreating (2 marks), operation condition (1 mark), reactions 2
  • marks and fuel quality improvement (2 marks))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the hydrodesulphurization process used in the production of Aviation Turbine Fuel, highlighting its role in improving fuel quality.
questions.solution_html:
• Fuel, highlighting its role in improving fuel quality.
  • The kerosene fraction obtained from atmospheric distillation is treated with hydrogen in the
  • presence of a suitable catalyst in a process known as hydrotreating. During this process, sulphur
  • compounds are converted into hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) and removed, while nitrogen and
  • oxygenated compounds are also eliminated. This purification step significantly enhances the
  • quality of the fuel by improving its thermal stability, which reduces gum and deposit formation
  • during high-temperature operation in turbine engines. Hydrotreating also increases the smoke
  • point, ensuring cleaner combustion, and improves the odour and colour of the fuel, making it
  • suitable for use as aviation turbine fuel (ATF) in accordance with aviation fuel specifications.
  • In some refineries, the Merox process is employed to oxidize and remove mercaptans
  • reducing fuel corrosiveness and improving odour. (Process explanation (4 marks) quality
  • improvement (3 marks))

questions.question: List the advantages and limitations of using SAF in modern aviation.
questions.solution_html:
• List the advantages and limitations of using SAF in modern aviation.
  • Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) offers several advantages in modern aviation. It significantly
  • reduces greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional jet fuel, helping to mitigate
  • climate change. SAF is produced from renewable resources such as biomass, waste oils, and
  • agricultural residues, promoting sustainability and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. It is
  • compatible with existing aircraft engines and infrastructure (drop-in fuel), requiring minimal
  • modifications. SAF also contains lower sulphur and aromatic content, resulting in cleaner
  • combustion, reduced particulate emissions, and improved air quality. Additionally, it supports
  • waste utilization and contributes to a circular economy.
  • However, SAF also has certain limitations. The high production cost makes it less
  • economically competitive than conventional fuels. There is limited large-scale availability due
  • to constraints in feedstock supply and production capacity. Some SAF pathways may face
  • feedstock sustainability issues and competition with food resources. The production processes
  • can be energy-intensive, and achieving consistent fuel quality can be challenging. Furthermore
  • widespread adoption requires policy support, infrastructure development, and technological
  • advancements. Thus, while SAF is environmentally beneficial, economic and scalability
  • challenges limit its current usage.
  • (Any 3 points from advantages and limitations give (3.5 marks) each)

questions.question: State the hydrotreating process used in the manufacture of ATF, including operating conditions, reactions involved, and improvements in fuel quality
questions.solution_html:
• conditions, reactions involved, and improvements in fuel quality.
  • Hydrotreating is a key refinery process used in the manufacture of aviation turbine fuel (ATF)
  • to improve its quality and ensure it meets strict aviation specifications. In this process, the
  • kerosene fraction obtained from crude oil distillation is mixed with hydrogen and passed over
  • a catalyst –molybdenum or nickel–molybdenum on alumina) at high
  • temperature and pressure. The hydrogen reacts with impurities such as sulphur, nitrogen
  • oxygen compounds, and unsaturated hydrocarbons, converting them into stable products like
  • hydrogen sulphide and ammonia, which are then removed. Hydrotreating improves the fuel’s
  • thermal stability, reduces corrosiveness, lowers sulphur content, and enhances combustion
  • characteristics. After the reaction, the treated fuel is cooled, gases are separated, and the
  • purified ATF is recovered, meeting the required standards for safe and efficient aircraft
  • operation. (statement about hydrotreating (2 marks), operation condition (1 mark), reactions 2
  • marks and fuel quality improvement (2 marks))

questions.question: Describe the hydrodesulphurization process used in the production of Aviation Turbine Fuel, highlighting its role in improving fuel quality.
questions.solution_html:
• Fuel, highlighting its role in improving fuel quality.
  • The kerosene fraction obtained from atmospheric distillation is treated with hydrogen in the
  • presence of a suitable catalyst in a process known as hydrotreating. During this process, sulphur
  • compounds are converted into hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) and removed, while nitrogen and
  • oxygenated compounds are also eliminated. This purification step significantly enhances the
  • quality of the fuel by improving its thermal stability, which reduces gum and deposit formation
  • during high-temperature operation in turbine engines. Hydrotreating also increases the smoke
  • point, ensuring cleaner combustion, and improves the odour and colour of the fuel, making it
  • suitable for use as aviation turbine fuel (ATF) in accordance with aviation fuel specifications.
  • In some refineries, the Merox process is employed to oxidize and remove mercaptans
  • reducing fuel corrosiveness and improving odour. (Process explanation (4 marks) quality
  • improvement (3 marks))
